The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed
Why, in plain words: A setting that shows shoppers their spending this month came on, and the code behind it likely fails when a shopper has bought nothing yet this month, so those shoppers' account pages returned errors.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 8m 37s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 40.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): at least 5,890.09 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: refused to act on a suspected cause - the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person - not taken
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #557 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 04:13 UTC, not back to normal by 04:21:37 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 04:50:08 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 04:19:49 UTC
Ended by: Argus: escalated to a person, Nov 11, 2026, 04:21:37 UTC - PR #557, opened as a draft

Summary
The service broke at 04:13 UTC and was not back to normal by 04:21:37 UTC, at least 8 minutes 37 seconds later. 30.8% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 40.5% failed. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by at least 5,890.09 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. A setting that shows shoppers their spending this month came on, and the code behind it likely fails when a shopper has bought nothing yet this month, so those shoppers' account pages returned errors. Argus handed the incident to a person. Argus did not test the first candidate it formed (C1): the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #557, for a person to review and merge. Account pages of shoppers who have not bought anything this month could keep failing while the monthly spend feature stays on, and the feature could come on again without any change showing in the flag provider's history.

Impact
at least 8m 37s - since onset, still not back to normal
40.5% - peak error rate
3,330 - requests failed
1.0% to 30.8% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
at least 5,890.09 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
With monthly-spend-feature on, the account page's spend summary runs average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides the shopper's spend this month by the number of purchases they made this month without handling a shopper who bought nothing this month, so for any shopper who has bought before but not this month the page raises ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed with server errors from the onset, and the account page error rate was at its highest at 04:19 UTC.
  Evidence:
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 33 occurrences in 37 minutes, 03:43–04:19; # was 0.50% to 40.50%, typically 1.00%, highest at 04:19
    AL1 Error rate above threshold for 5m
why 1 Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 during 04:13–04:19 UTC. This error did not appear in the log lines before the onset.
  Evidence:
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 13 occurrences in 7 minutes, 04:13–04:19
why 2 The monthly-spend-feature flag was off for every evaluation during 03:43–04:12 UTC. It was on for part of the evaluations at 04:13 UTC (on 66, off 134 of 200) and on for every evaluation during 04:14–04:19 UTC. Neither the production change events read at 04:20:15 UTC nor the flag provider's history read at 04:20:17 UTC shows this change, so the record does not show what switched the flag. All replicas ran the same revision when read at 04:20:15 UTC, but the record does not show whether that revision was already running before the onset, so a change to it was not ruled out.
  Evidence:
    G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 03:43–04:12
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 134 / on 66 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 04:13
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 04:14–04:19
    T8 04:20:15 Investigator Agent: Read back 0 production changes
    T14 04:20:17 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 04:20:17
    T9 04:20:15 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
  Ruled out:
    The client-disconnect failures on account pages: they were logged well before the onset while the account page error rate stayed at its usual 1%, and they stopped at the onset.
      G46bc ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 48 occurrences in 31 minutes, 03:43–04:13
      Gbac1
    A deploy, release or flag change on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 11 04:14; the Investigator Agent read back 0 production changes. A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 04:20:17.
      T7
      T8
      T14
why 3 With the flag on, the account page runs average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides by the number of purchases the shopper made this month and fails for a shopper who has bought before but not this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
    G5309
Contributing factors
- No check was seen that ran the spend summary with monthly-spend-feature on for a shopper with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on for shoppers. (AI-3)
- The flag went from on for part of the evaluations to on for all of them by the next minute. No rollout stage was seen that held or reversed it as account page errors rose. (AI-4)
- The flag coming on did not appear in the flag provider's history or in the production change events, so the change was not in the record of what changed. (AI-5, AI-6)
- No on-call incident was linked to the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop, so nobody was paged. (AI-7)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched from off to on at about 04:13. With it on, the account page's spend summary code hits a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate rose from about 1% to about 33%. No deployment, config change or rollout split is recorded, and the replicas did not move. | 0.93 | never tried: the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person

Trigger
No trigger was established.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
 | 04:20:21 | Refused to act on C1 - the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person | Argus | nothing to put back | not taken
 | 04:21:37 | Proposed a fix: PR #557 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 04:13 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 04:19:25 UTC, 6 minutes 25 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #557 | open
AI-2 | Turn monthly-spend-feature off on io-shop until the fix in PR #557 is merged and deployed. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Before any feature flag on io-shop can be enabled in production, require tests that run the code behind the flag with the flag on, including the case of a shopper with no purchases in the current period. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Roll out flags such as monthly-spend-feature in stages that pause and switch the flag back off automatically when the account page error rate rises. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Find out how monthly-spend-feature came on with no change in the flag provider's history or in the production change events. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Make every change to io-shop feature flags go through the flag provider so that the change appears in its history. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Link the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to on-call paging so that a person is paged when it fires. | detect | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 52 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 56 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus refused to act on C1 - the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person.
- 2 minutes 12 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #557.
What went wrong
Nothing.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)

Response effort
none - engineer time
288,753 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/2b192af8-ca6a-4694-b004-1bbd425275df
The fix it proposed: PR #557 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/557) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G7e5d | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 03:43–04:12
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 48 occurrences in 31 minutes, 03:43–04:13
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 33 occurrences in 37 minutes, 03:43–04:19; # was 0.50% to 40.50%, typically 1.00%, highest at 04:19
Gad41 | INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 4 occurrences in 6 minutes, 04:03–04:08
G971b | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 134 / on 66 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 04:13
G5309 | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 13 occurrences in 7 minutes, 04:13–04:19
Gce95 | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 04:14–04:19
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | average_spend_per_item_this_month divided total_this_month_cents by the number of purchases in the current month. That number is zero for any shopper who has bought before but not this month, which is a common case. The test fixtures even call it "the ordinary case". With monthly-spend-feature off, this code never runs. As the flag rolled out to 100%, every such shopper's account page raised ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, which is why the error rate rose step by step as the rollout progressed.

The fix: when nothing was bought this month, the monthly average is 0 (the shopper spent nothing across zero items), and the function returns 0 without dividing. The return type stays int, so callers are unaffected. Nothing changes for shoppers who did buy this month. With the flag off, the page still shows the lifetime figure. The lifetime average still raises for an account with no purchases at all. That behaviour is deliberate and has its own test, so I left it alone. Errors are not swallowed: the only change is that the empty case is now handled explicitly. A regression test reproduces the incident's input through render_spend_summary with the flag on. On the current code that test raises ZeroDivisionError.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist

○ Impact assessed (for a person)
  the loss is measured to the close; when the service is back to normal is for a person to report
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)

○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:
overview: On io-shop, account pages failed for some shoppers for {duration}. A setting that shows shoppers how much they have spent this month was switched on. The code behind it likely fails when a shopper has bought nothing yet this month, so those shoppers got errors instead of their account pages. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests failed. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in sales. Nobody was paged, so no one was called in to respond. Argus did not undo the suspected cause because that change does not appear in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person. Argus also proposed a fix, which is open as a draft and has not been put into use.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
